acceptance.duplicate_gate: Versioned domain-tagged semantic-core key derived before writes; best-effort repository search returned zero matches. Duplicate means no event, no CURRENT update, no Slack.
acceptance.pointer_gate: After the stale call returned 409 and CURRENT readback remained exact v36/blob cb8f5eb533cf60c0701a4b37e51a2d4bd9c851d9/digest 8a8b5581a4d7aeb1b53a3d49fb648e68d742fc1b2e63080fceb7e52a5bbec019: commit and read back this event; fetch CURRENT again; update only with that exact blob SHA; read back CURRENT, this event, and predecessor.
acceptance.slack_rule: Post once only after v37 advances; combine version advance and observed conflict. No changed accepted transition means silence.
acceptance.stale_rule: Exactly one stale update_file call used v35 blob 0ce1a5863d5fe3b91e87d189316afa1f52d57c4c with bytes identical to observed v36. HTTP 409 is reject; no unconditional retry.

experiment.controlled_factor: Replace C4's local-only stale comparison with one actual stale GitHub Contents API call; keep all accepted-transition gates unchanged.
experiment.hypothesis: The per-file Contents API blob-SHA precondition rejects the immediately prior CURRENT blob after the file advances, without changing current bytes. This is a one-file stale-write guard, not a database transaction.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: Stale call succeeds or changes CURRENT; post-conflict readback differs; duplicate key existed; exact second read changes before update; digest recomputation fails; or final chain bindings disagree.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: One serial stale call used a prior blob SHA and replacement bytes identical to current. It demonstrates one HTTP 409 mismatch at one file and moment, not overlapping writers, divergent payloads, retry behavior, linearizability, serializable isolation, cross-file atomicity, database durability, exactly-once execution, Slack atomicity, server-side idempotency uniqueness, or automatic orphan repair. Event, CURRENT, reads, and Slack remain separate effects.
canonical_transition.rollback: Append a compensating event from the then-current version; never delete this event or Slack message; replace CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
